newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds close lower.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds close lower.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds and Makams closed lower on Wednesday in response to a month of steadily declining yields, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.06 pct to 172.15
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: -0.02 pct to 162.12
Volume was moderate at 147 million shekels with dollar-linked bonds rising sharply but on very low volume.
"CPI-linked bonds closed slightly higher today because of nice rise in short bonds, while long bonds were mixed," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.

Uri Schur, of Eyal Securities, said the drop in unlinked bond prices came in response to low yields. "During the last month yields on unlinked bonds fell sharply. They are less attractive now," he said.

Prices for unlinked Makams also fell in response to several weeks of declining yields. "With today's decline yields recovered a little, rising to 14.46 percent from 14.28 percent on Tuesday," the Mizrahi trader said.

The Bank of Israel said on Wednesday that it is relying on its Makam certificates as the chief weapon in countering the government's expansionary fiscal policy. The bank said the value of Makam certificates held by the public grew to 18.7 billion shekels as of November, compared with just 6.26 billion shekels at the end of 1994.
Dollar-linked bonds continued to rise in thin trading, following the U.S. currency's strength in the local currency market.
"Dollar-linked bonds are expected to decline on Thursday following the decline of dollar in the European markets," the Mizrahi trader said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
